one_line: Maharajas of Mysore guiding social reform, industrial modernity and integration into the Indian Union.

appearance.age_look: Krishnaraja appears in his late 30s with a dignified medium build; Jayachamarajendra appears in his early 30s, slightly taller and leaner.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with wheatish-brown complexions and neatly groomed moustaches; Krishnaraja’s eyes are calm and thoughtful with a gentle, composed default expression, while Jayachamarajendra’s eyes are sharper with a focused, determined default expression.
appearance.hair: Both keep their natural black hair short and tidy beneath royal headgear; Krishnaraja wears a tall Mysore-style bejewelled turban in deep maroon velvet with a central white feather plume and gold band, while Jayachamarajendra wears a lower-profile cream silk turban with a subtle gold border and a small central jewel ornament.
appearance.costume: They share a coordinated yet distinct royal-constitutional look: Krishnaraja wears a rich maroon silk angarakha-style long coat with subtle gold woven buta motifs, reaching just below the knee, over an ivory churidar, a gold-embroidered sash (patka) draped diagonally from right shoulder to left hip, and pointed leather mojari shoes; Jayachamarajendra wears a deep navy blue bandhgala (closed-neck) coat with brass buttons and a faint pinstripe texture over cream churidar trousers, a narrow maroon cummerbund at the waist, and polished black jodhpuri shoes; both have simple, dignified jewellery—slim gold bracelets, a single signet ring, and a modest pearl necklace—avoiding excessive ornamentation.
appearance.signature: A single elegant leather-bound portfolio folder emblazoned with a small gold Mysore emblem, held most often by Jayachamarajendra and occasionally passed between them, symbolising committee reports, industrial charters and the Instrument of Accession.

ref_desc: Two Mysore maharajas stand together, both wheatish oval-faced men with neat moustaches, Krishnaraja in a maroon angarakha, ivory churidar and tall maroon jeweled turban, Jayachamarajendra in a navy bandhgala, cream churidar and cream turban, sharing a brown leather portfolio with gold emblem.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two royal men from early 20th-century Mysore standing side by side: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV is a dignified, medium-built man in his late 30s with an oval wheatish-brown face, calm eyes and a neat moustache, wearing a tall deep maroon velvet Mysore turban with a gold band and white feather plume, a rich maroon silk angarakha-style long coat patterned with subtle gold buta motifs, an ivory churidar, a diagonally draped gold-embroidered sash from right shoulder to left hip, slim gold bracelet, single signet ring, modest pearl necklace, and pointed brown leather mojari shoes; beside him Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar is slightly taller and leaner, early 30s, with a similar oval wheatish face but sharper, determined eyes and a neat moustache, wearing a cream silk turban with a narrow gold border and small central jewel, a deep navy blue bandhgala coat with brass buttons and faint pinstripe texture, cream churidar trousers, a narrow maroon cummerbund, polished black jodhpuri shoes, slim gold bracelet, signet ring, and modest pearl necklace; have them prominently hold together one elegant brown leather-bound portfolio folder stamped with a small gold Mysore emblem, with consistent deep maroon, navy blue, cream, gold and ivory colours across both outfits, shown front, three-quarter and back views in a clean reference-style layout.
